title: Small Favours
subtitle: One small favour leads to another

quests.title: Just a Loaf
text: Bram the baker would gladly give you a loaf for the road, if he had any flour.

lines: A loaf? For the road? Oh, I'd love to! I'd love to! But there's no flour!
None! Not a pinch! I checked the sack four times. It's a catastrophe!
The windmill's stopped turning. If the mill stops, the bread stops, and if the bread stops... I can't say it.
Would you go and ask Hesk what's wrong? Oh, you would? You're a hero!
It's just one small favour.

quests.title: Torn Sails
text: Miller Hesk is standing under his windmill, looking at it.

lines: Oh. Hello. Sorry. Bram sent you? Sorry about Bram.
The storm... it tore the sails. Clean through. I can't grind a thing.
New sails need canvas. Canvas means Nell. I'd ask her myself, only... she frightens me a little.
Would you ask Nell? If it's not too much trouble. Sorry.
One small favour, that's all.

quests.title: The Broken Shuttle
text: Nell the weaver would weave canvas this minute, if her loom worked.

lines: Stop. Wipe your feet. Both of them. Now step on the mat. The middle.
Canvas? Of course. Except my shuttle snapped this morning, at seven minutes past six, and nothing has been right since.
Olsen could carve me a new one. Tell him the exact length. I've written it down. Twice.
And bring me straw while you're at it. Sixteen bundles. Not fifteen. Sixteen.
Just a small favour.

quests.title: Only the Old Birch Will Do
text: Olsen the carpenter will carve a shuttle. Eventually. He has standards.

lines: A shuttle? From ordinary birch? Absolutely not.
Young birch grows too fast. All sap and no sense. It'll warp before the season's out.
Only the old birches past the woods will do. The ones with the bees. Roots deep in good black soil, the way trees ought to grow.
Fell them clean, with an axe. None of that gadgetry. Do it right or don't do it.
Eight logs, no stings. It's a very small favour, really.

quests.title: Shuttle, Canvas, Sails
text: Now everything can happen in the right order. Take the shuttle to Nell, and the canvas to Hesk.

lines: My shuttle! Let me measure it. ...Exactly right. To the hair. Infuriating.
He's insufferable, but lovely work.
Here's your canvas. Folded in eight. Keep it folded in eight. Off you go to Hesk.
tasks.title: Bring Nell the shuttle

lines: Canvas? For me? Oh. Oh, thank you. Give me an hour.
...There. Sails on, mill turning. Listen to it.
One bag of flour, as promised. I hope it's enough. Sorry if it isn't.
tasks.title: Bring Hesk the canvas

quests.title: The Fox and the Flour
text: On the road back to Reece, something small and orange snatches the flour bag and bolts.

encounter.name: Flour Thief
lines: *The fox drops the flour bag, eyeing your berries.*
*It takes the berries and trots off, very pleased with itself.*
Is that... is that flour? Real flour? I think I'm going to cry. I am crying.
You're a marvel! A legend! I'll name a bun after you!
One crusty loaf, as promised. And a breadbox, since you went to all that trouble.
And three loaves, actually. Four's too many. Three's perfect. Oh, best day ever!
Next time I ask a small favour, you have my permission to run.

quests.title: The Ferryman's Fee
text: Gil the ferryman will row anyone across to the island village, for a fee.

lines: Island village? Sure, I'll row you. Fare's a favour, as ever.
Well. Not quite a favour this time. I'd like a good fishing net.
Mine's more hole than net. Ada up the lake shore makes the best in the country.
Next village along. Tell her Gil sent you. She'll sigh. Everyone sighs at me.
It's a small favour. The lake isn't going anywhere.

quests.title: Out of Rope
text: Ada can knot a net blindfolded. She's out of rope.

lines: Gil's net? Gil owes me for the last one. In favours. I have a drawer of them.
I'll do it, but I'm out of rope. Rope means flax, and flax means Tamsin.
Farmer Tamsin, in the village round the lake. Mind the beans.
Tell her I'll swap a net for a sheaf. She'll grumble. Mind the mesh.
tasks.title: Ask Ada about the net

quests.title: The Scarecrow's Hat
text: Farmer Tamsin won't spare a stalk until her scarecrow has its hat back.

lines: Flax? From me? Not a stalk. Not till he has his hat.
A witch's black cat ran off with it into the swamp. Nobody goes near that hut, and I don't blame them.
You look brave. Or daft. Either'll do. Go and get it.
He feels it, you know. The bareness.

quests.title: A Witch's Bargain
text: The witch will give the hat back, for a pot of proper black tea brewed in a copper kettle. She's very particular about the kettle.

lines: Tea? In a copper kettle? Oh, you do know the old ways.
Hat? Yes, the cat brought it. He's very proud of himself. Terrible creature.
Take it. And tell the scarecrow I said he looks better with it.
Now go away before I put the kettle back on.
tasks.title: Trade the tea to the witch

rewards.name: The Scarecrow's Hat
lore: A faded hat, slightly chewed by a cat.

quests.title: Hat, Flax, Rope
text: Return the hat to its scarecrow, and Tamsin gives you a sheaf of flax. Twist it into rope and take it to Ada, who knots the net while you wait.

lines: My scarecrow's hat! Chewed, but his. Look at him. He's glowing.
Flax, as promised. A whole sheaf. Don't tread on it.
Tell Ada the rope's on me. Honest work, that.
tasks.title: Return the hat to Tamsin

lines: Rope! Good, strong rope. Sit down. Don't touch the mesh.
...There. A proper net, knotted while you waited.
Give it to Gil. Tell him it's the last one I do on credit.
tasks.title: Take the rope to Ada

quests.title: The Crossing
text: Gil takes the net, keeps his word and rows you out to the island village. Halfway across, the drowned come up around the boat.

lines: Ada's net! Look at the weave. She's forgiven me, I think.
A deal's a deal. Hop in, mind the wet bit.
...Funny. The lake's gone quiet. It's never quiet.

encounter.name: Drowned
lines: *A drowned lurches up beside the boat.*

encounter.name: Drowned
lines: *Another drowned climbs out of the water.*
